dream.gunpowder.title: The fire powder
dream.gunpowder.intro: In your dream you sit in a bright room with a formula on the board; the teacher taps the chalk: "Black powder. Three substances. Who remembers the proportion?"
dream.gunpowder.q1.1: What is fire powder made of? Mark everything needed — and nothing extra.
dream.gunpowder.q1.2: In what proportions should you mix what you chose? Enter percentages — they must add up to 100.
dream.gunpowder.q2.1: Where will you get all this in your world? Mark where the needed things come from.
dream.gunpowder.q3.1: A sage, the ruler's adviser, smirks: "You say this can break a wall? Our wall is {wall} m high. A ladder leans at 30° to the wall. How long must the ladder be to reach the top?"
dream.gunpowder.q3.2: "And how will you make it? Name the order of work." Put the steps in order and remove the extra one.
dream.gunpowder.hint1: Chemistry textbook, grade 8: there are three substances in gunpowder, and one of them makes up more than half.
dream.gunpowder.hint2: In the old days saltpeter was gathered where manure rots; sulfur came from volcanoes.
dream.gunpowder.hint3: A right triangle: hypotenuse = leg / cos of the angle between them.
dream.gunpowder.breakthrough: The powder flared with such a roar that the guards came running. A month later you were summoned to court: every ruler needs a master of fire.
dream.gunpowder.partial: The powder burns, hisses and spits sparks, but it won't break a wall. Still, your fireworks were the best at the festival — and well paid.
dream.gunpowder.failure: The mixture didn't catch — or caught the wrong way. Burnt hands, laughing neighbors and a rumor that you deal with dark powers.
dream.gunpowder.death: The mixture flared in your hands. The blast was heard on the next street.
dream.gunpowder.known: The masters just shrugged: fire powder has been known here for a long time. Inventing what's already invented is a skill too.
dream.gunpowder.truth: Black powder is 75% saltpeter, 15% charcoal and 10% sulfur. Chinese alchemists invented it around the 9th century while searching for an elixir of immortality. It reached the Islamic world and Europe in the 13th century, and Rus by the late 14th.
dream.gunpowder.opt.nitre_bed: a nitre bed: manure, urine and ash for months, then leach it
dream.gunpowder.opt.volcano_sulfur: sulfur from merchants who bring it from volcanoes
dream.gunpowder.opt.corn: press through a sieve into grains
dream.gunpowder.opt.heat_mix: heat the mixture over a fire
dream.clean_hands.title: Childbirth without fever
dream.clean_hands.intro: You dream of a hospital ward — white and bright. The teacher's voice: "Why did women die of childbed fever in some maternity wards but not in others?"
dream.clean_hands.q1.1: What saves a mother from childbed fever? Mark everything needed.
dream.clean_hands.q2.1: What will you take for it from your own house?
dream.clean_hands.q3.1: Before, one mother in {die} died. If hands are washed and cloths boiled, deaths become {k} times fewer. How many mothers out of 100 will survive?
dream.clean_hands.hint1: Biology, grade 8: infection is carried by hands and dirty linen.
dream.clean_hands.hint2: Lye is ash soaked in water.
dream.clean_hands.hint3: Count how many died out of 100, divide by the factor — and subtract from 100.
dream.clean_hands.breakthrough: In your district mothers stopped dying of fever. The midwives laughed at first, then started doing as you do. Noble families call for you — and pay in gold.
dream.clean_hands.partial: You convinced at least your own family: now they wash hands and boil swaddling cloths. The neighbors look askance, but some copy you.
dream.clean_hands.failure: No one listened: "washing hands before a birth — what nonsense." The midwives complain to the elders.
dream.clean_hands.truth: Washing hands in chlorinated lime was introduced by the Hungarian doctor Ignaz Semmelweis in 1847: deaths of mothers in his clinic fell from 10–18% to 1–2%. His colleagues mocked him; he was proven right only after Pasteur's discoveries.
dream.clean_hands.opt.wash_hands: wash hands with lye or lime
dream.clean_hands.opt.close_windows: close the windows and never air the room
dream.rehydration.title: The flux plague
dream.rehydration.intro: You dream of a lesson: the teacher holds a glass of water. "People die not of diarrhea itself but because water and salt leave the body. What should the sick drink?"
dream.rehydration.q1.1: For {liters} L of boiled water — how many teaspoons of sugar?
dream.rehydration.q1.2: And how many teaspoons of salt for the same {liters} L?
dream.rehydration.q2.1: You may have no sugar. What can replace it?
dream.rehydration.q3.1: How do you give the sick person drink? Put in order, remove the extra.
dream.rehydration.hint1: Biology, grade 8: six spoons of something sweet and half a spoon of salt per liter.
dream.rehydration.hint2: Anything with sugar or starch will do.
dream.rehydration.hint3: First make the water safe, then let it cool.
dream.rehydration.breakthrough: Your drink pulled dozens of people back from the brink during the flux plague. Healers copy the recipe, and noble houses call you to their children.
dream.rehydration.partial: You nursed your own family through it. The neighbors didn't believe you — but they remembered.
dream.rehydration.failure: The drink didn't help — maybe wrong amounts, maybe too late.
dream.rehydration.truth: Oral rehydration solution — 6 teaspoons of sugar and ½ teaspoon of salt per liter of boiled water — was introduced in the 1960s. The Lancet called it possibly the most important medical advance of the 20th century: it has saved tens of millions of children.
dream.rehydration.opt.sip_often: give it often, in small sips
dream.rehydration.opt.no_drink: give no drink so it "dries up"
dream.scurvy.title: Scurvy
dream.scurvy.intro: You dream of a ship: the sailors' gums bleed and their teeth are loose. The teacher asks: "What are they missing?"
dream.scurvy.q1.1: What saves from scurvy? Mark everything needed.
dream.scurvy.q2.1: Which of these can you take from your port on a long voyage?
dream.scurvy.q3.1: How do you ferment cabbage so it lasts {days} days at sea? Put the steps in order, remove the extra.
dream.scurvy.hint1: Biology, grade 9: vitamin C is in fresh fruit, greens and sauerkraut.
dream.scurvy.hint2: Pine needle tea helps too — northerners knew it.
dream.scurvy.breakthrough: The ships that took your cabbage and lemons came back without scurvy. Shipowners and merchants argue over who takes you as a partner first.
dream.scurvy.partial: Those who listened came back healthy, those who didn't — with bleeding gums. Your name is known in the port.
dream.scurvy.failure: They laughed at you: "cabbage doesn't cure scurvy." The sailors left with salt beef and biscuits.
dream.scurvy.truth: Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C. In 1747 the Scottish doctor James Lind proved by experiment that lemons and oranges cure it. Captain Cook took sauerkraut on his voyages — and lost not a single sailor to scurvy.
dream.scurvy.opt.weight_cool: weigh it down — and keep it cool
dream.cowpox.title: Inoculation against smallpox
dream.cowpox.intro: You dream of a lesson on the history of medicine: milkmaids never caught smallpox. "Why?" asks the teacher.
dream.cowpox.q1.1: What do you take to inoculate against smallpox?
dream.cowpox.q3.1: The court physician objects: "Cut healthy people? First tell me how you do it." Put the steps in order, remove the extra.
dream.cowpox.q3.2: "Now prove that it works": of 100 uninoculated people {sick} fell ill, of 100 inoculated — one. How many times less do the inoculated fall ill?
dream.cowpox.hint1: Biology, grade 8: cowpox protects against human smallpox.
dream.cowpox.hint2: Who most often catches cowpox — those who milk cows.
dream.cowpox.hint3: Divide one number by the other.
dream.cowpox.breakthrough: You inoculated your family first, then the neighbors. When the plague came, your street barely noticed it. The ruler ordered the court inoculated — and rewarded you.
dream.cowpox.partial: You inoculated your own, and smallpox passed your house by. Others fear the "cow disease."
dream.cowpox.failure: The inoculation didn't take, and you were accused of spreading the disease.
dream.cowpox.death: You inoculated yourself with the wrong thing. Smallpox came to your house first.
dream.cowpox.known: Here people already know how to guard against smallpox: they inoculate with a scab from the sick (variolation). Your way is safer — but you can't call it new.
dream.cowpox.truth: In 1796 the English doctor Edward Jenner inoculated a boy with cowpox — and the boy did not catch smallpox. Hence the word "vaccine" (Latin vacca, cow). In China from the 16th century people were inoculated with material from smallpox patients, which was more dangerous.
dream.cowpox.opt.burnt_clothes: ash of a sick person's burnt clothes
dream.cowpox.opt.cut_shoulder: a shallow cut on the shoulder
dream.penicillin.title: The healing mold
dream.penicillin.intro: You dream of a laboratory and a forgotten dish: around a patch of mold there is a clean ring. "What is it killing?" asks the teacher.
dream.penicillin.q2.1: How do you grow the medicine? Put the steps in order, remove the extra.
dream.penicillin.q3.1: One jug gives medicine for 1/{part} of a single wound. How many jugs do you need for {wounded} wounded?
dream.penicillin.hint1: Biology: the blue-green mold, like on an old orange.
dream.penicillin.hint2: Mold likes warmth; the finished medicine must not be heated.
dream.penicillin.hint3: Multiply the wounded by the jugs each one needs.
dream.penicillin.breakthrough: After the battle, the wounded you treated survived three times as often. You were taken to the army — with pay and honor.
dream.penicillin.partial: The medicine helped two out of five — a miracle even so. Word about you spread.
dream.penicillin.failure: Your mold was the wrong kind — the wound festered.
dream.penicillin.death: You fussed with rot and caught the infection yourself.
dream.penicillin.truth: In 1928 the Scot Alexander Fleming noticed that Penicillium mold kills bacteria. Florey and Chain turned it into a medicine in the 1940s; penicillin saved millions of wounded in the Second World War.
dream.penicillin.opt.bluegreen_mold: blue-green mold from an orange, melon or bread
dream.penicillin.opt.apply_now: apply to the wound at once
dream.rotation.title: Four fields
dream.rotation.intro: You dream of a lesson: four fields on the board and arrows going round. "Why did some villages starve and others didn't?"
dream.rotation.q1.1: In what order should you sow one field year after year? Arrange, remove the extra.
dream.rotation.q2.1: Which plant of your land gives strength back to the soil?
dream.rotation.q3.1: You sowed {sacks} sacks. The harvest was threefold, now it's fivefold. How many more sacks did you reap?
dream.rotation.hint1: Biology, grade 6: legumes enrich the soil with nitrogen.
dream.rotation.hint2: Think about what grows here and now.
dream.rotation.hint3: Threefold — you reap three times what you sow.
dream.rotation.breakthrough: Within three years your fields yielded twice as much as your neighbors'. The lord gave you the best land, and the neighbors came to learn.
dream.rotation.partial: The harvest grew, if not twofold. You no longer go hungry in bad years.
dream.rotation.failure: You sowed the wrong thing — and the year was wasted.
dream.rotation.truth: The Norfolk four-course rotation (wheat → turnips → barley → clover) was introduced in England in the 18th century and became a basis of the agricultural revolution. In the Middle Ages Europe and Rus used the three-field system.
dream.thales.title: The height of the temple
dream.thales.intro: You dream of a geometry lesson: the shadow of a pole and the shadow of a pyramid. "How do you measure the height without climbing up?"
dream.thales.q1.1: You are {h} m tall, your shadow is {me} m, the temple's shadow is {tower} m. How tall is the temple?
dream.thales.q3.1: At what angle above the horizon must the sun stand for a shadow to equal the object's height? (in degrees)
dream.thales.hint2: You need something of known length and level ground.
dream.thales.breakthrough: Priests and builders were amazed that you measured the temple without climbing it. You were taken on as a builder — with honor and pay.
dream.thales.partial: You guessed the height almost exactly — and won a ten-coin bet.
dream.thales.failure: You were off by a good ten cubits — they laughed at you.
dream.thales.known: They already know this here: "Thales knew it," said the old builder.
dream.thales.truth: According to legend, Thales of Miletus around 600 BC measured the height of an Egyptian pyramid by its shadow — at the hour when a man's shadow equals his height. It's a property of similar triangles.
dream.right_angle.title: The builder's right angle
dream.right_angle.intro: You dream of a lesson: a triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 on the board. "How did ancient builders set walls at right angles?"
dream.right_angle.q1.1: The two legs are {a} and {b} cubits. How long is the hypotenuse?
dream.right_angle.q2.1: How many equal parts must a rope have to form a 3–4–5 triangle?
dream.right_angle.q3.1: A square courtyard has a side of {side} m. How long is its diagonal?
dream.right_angle.hint2: Add up the sides of the triangle.
dream.right_angle.hint3: A square's diagonal is the side times the square root of two.
dream.right_angle.breakthrough: Your walls stood straight as a string. Contractors fight over you.
dream.right_angle.partial: The corners came out almost square. The owners are pleased.
dream.right_angle.failure: The wall went crooked. The owner demands you redo it at your own cost.
dream.right_angle.known: Builders here have known this since ancient times: every crew has a knotted rope.
dream.right_angle.truth: The 3–4–5 triple was known to the Babylonians (the Plimpton 322 tablet, about 1800 BC), Egyptians, Indians and Chinese. The proof of the theorem is attributed to Pythagoras (6th century BC).
dream.eratosthenes.title: The circumference of the Earth
dream.eratosthenes.intro: You dream of a lesson: a globe and two wells. "In one city at noon the sun looks straight down the well. And in the other?"
dream.eratosthenes.q1.1: At noon the sun is overhead in one city; in another a pole casts a shadow at {angle}°. The cities are {dist} km apart. What is the Earth's circumference?
dream.eratosthenes.q2.1: What do you need to measure it?
dream.eratosthenes.q3.1: The sage objects: "If the Earth is a ball, how many days would it take to walk around it, if a caravan covers {pace} km a day?" (take the circumference as 40,000 km)
dream.eratosthenes.q3.2: "And what shape is the Earth's shadow on the Moon during an eclipse?"
dream.eratosthenes.hint1: The angle is to 360° as the distance is to the circumference.
dream.eratosthenes.hint2: The same moment in two places.
dream.eratosthenes.hint3: Think which shadow only a sphere casts.
dream.eratosthenes.breakthrough: You out-argued the sages. You're invited to be court astronomer, and scribes copy your calculations.
dream.eratosthenes.partial: The sages grew thoughtful — and invited you to their discussions. They pay well for them.
dream.eratosthenes.failure: The sages mocked you: "The Earth is flat as a pancake, anyone can see that."
dream.eratosthenes.death: You were accused of heresy. The trial was short.
dream.eratosthenes.known: Here they've long known the Earth is round; you only repeated the ancients.
dream.eratosthenes.truth: Eratosthenes in Egypt around 240 BC compared noon shadows in Syene and Alexandria (7.2°, 5,000 stadia) and got a circumference of about 40,000 km — nearly exact. Aristotle had already noted the Earth's round shadow on the Moon.
dream.eratosthenes.opt.caravan_distance: the distance by caravan or by paces
dream.archimedes.title: The ruler's crown
dream.archimedes.intro: You dream of a physics lesson: a bath, water spilling over the edge. "How do you check whether the jeweler mixed in silver?"
dream.archimedes.q1.1: The crown weighs {m} kg and displaces {v} cm³ of water. What is its density (g/cm³)? Pure gold is 19.3.
dream.archimedes.q2.1: What will you measure it with?
dream.archimedes.q3.1: If the crown is gold (19.3 g/cm³) mixed with silver (10.5 g/cm³), how much gold is in it by weight (in %)?
dream.archimedes.hint1: Density is mass divided by volume; 1 kg = 1000 g.
dream.archimedes.hint2: You need both the weight and the volume.
dream.archimedes.hint3: Add up the volumes of gold and silver: 1/density = share/19.3 + (1 − share)/10.5.
dream.archimedes.breakthrough: The jeweler confessed to the fraud. The ruler made you keeper of the mint.
dream.archimedes.partial: You proved the crown impure but couldn't say how much. The ruler is generous all the same.
dream.archimedes.failure: Your test proved nothing — the ruler is displeased.
dream.archimedes.known: Here children are told this story: "Eureka!"
dream.archimedes.truth: According to legend, Archimedes (3rd century BC) solved the riddle of King Hiero's crown by getting into a bath — and ran out shouting "Eureka!". The law of buoyancy bears his name.
dream.archimedes.opt.full_vessel: a vessel filled to the brim
dream.archimedes.opt.overflow_bowl: a bowl to catch the overflow
dream.lever.title: Lever and pulleys
dream.lever.intro: You dream of a lesson: "Give me a place to stand and I will move the Earth." A lever and a stone on the board.
dream.lever.q1.1: The stone weighs {w} kg, the lever is {L} m long, the fulcrum is {a} m from the stone. How much force (in kg) must you press on the long end?
dream.lever.q2.1: A pulley with four strands, a load of {q} kg. How much force (in kg) is needed?
dream.lever.q3.1: Build a hoist: put the steps in order, remove the extra.
dream.lever.hint1: The law of the lever, grade 7: force × arm = load × arm.
dream.lever.hint2: Each strand holds its share of the load.
dream.lever.hint3: First the support, then the blocks, then the rope.
dream.lever.breakthrough: You raised a bell to the belfry that forty men couldn't lift. You were called to build for the ruler.
dream.lever.partial: The hoist works, though it creaks. The crew pays you double.
dream.lever.failure: The rope snapped and the load crashed down. Luckily no one was standing below.
dream.lever.death: The load broke loose — right onto you.
dream.lever.known: They've known this here since the days of Archimedes.
dream.lever.truth: Archimedes formulated the law of the lever in the 3rd century BC. The Romans built pulleys and treadwheel cranes; that's how stones for temples and cathedrals were raised.
dream.interest.title: Money that grows
dream.interest.intro: You dream of a lesson: "Why did bankers grow rich without making anything?" — and a table of percentages.
dream.interest.q1.1: {p} coins were lent at {r}% a year for {n} years. How much comes back (with interest on interest)?
dream.interest.q2.1: A gambler's sense will help too: which sum of two dice comes up most often?
dream.interest.q2.2: In how many cases out of 36 does this sum come up?
dream.interest.q3.1: How do you keep books so no one cheats you? Put the steps in order, remove the extra.
dream.interest.hint1: Each year the sum is multiplied by (1 + the rate).
dream.interest.hint3: Every deal is written down twice.
dream.interest.breakthrough: Your books balance to the coin, and your money works. You're invited to be a banker; nobles ask you for loans.
dream.interest.partial: You made extra — and didn't let anyone cheat you.
dream.interest.failure: You got lost in the sums — and were cheated.
dream.interest.known: They already keep books this way here: "That's Italian bookkeeping."
dream.interest.truth: Double-entry bookkeeping was described by Luca Pacioli in 1494, but in Italy it was used around 1300. Compound interest was known in Babylon; that 7 is the most frequent sum of two dice was worked out by Cardano in the 16th century.
dream.interest.opt.two_sides: income and expenses on different sides of the book
dream.lenses.title: Glasses for the old
dream.lenses.intro: You dream of an optics lesson: a lens gathers the sun's rays into a point. "How do you help a grandfather who can't see the letters?"
dream.lenses.q1.1: Which glass will help a long-sighted old man read?
dream.lenses.q2.1: What can it be made of here and now?
dream.lenses.q3.1: The glass has a focal length of {f} m. What is its optical power in diopters?
dream.lenses.hint2: Think about what exists in your country at all.
dream.lenses.breakthrough: An old scholar read a letter — for the first time in ten years. Glassmakers and nobles line up at your door.
dream.lenses.partial: The lenses came out a bit cloudy, but grandfather is happy.
dream.lenses.failure: The lenses only made his eyes worse.
dream.lenses.known: Spectacles are already made here — in Venice glassmakers grind them.
dream.lenses.truth: Spectacles with convex lenses appeared in Italy around 1286. The diopter as a unit of optical power was introduced in 1872 by the French ophthalmologist Ferdinand Monoyer.
dream.latitude.title: The Pole Star
dream.latitude.intro: You dream of a lesson: a globe, parallels and a star above the pole. "How did sailors know where they were?"
dream.latitude.q1.1: The Pole Star stands {star}° above the horizon. What is your latitude?
dream.latitude.q2.1: The star has risen by {deg}°. How many kilometers farther north are you?
dream.latitude.q3.1: What will you make an instrument from to measure the star's height?
dream.latitude.hint1: The height of the Pole Star equals the latitude.
dream.latitude.hint2: One degree of latitude is about 111 km.
dream.latitude.hint3: Arab sailors made do with a board and a rope.
dream.latitude.breakthrough: Your ship came into port right on time while others went astray. Shipowners want you as pilot, merchants as a partner.
dream.latitude.partial: You didn't lose your way — and that's a lot.
dream.latitude.failure: You led the ship off course. You barely made it back.
dream.latitude.death: The ship broke up on the rocks — your reckoning was wrong.
dream.latitude.known: Pilots here have long sailed this way — with a kamal.
dream.latitude.truth: Arab sailors (with the kamal — a board on a knotted cord) and Europeans (with the quadrant and astrolabe) used the Pole Star's height above the horizon to find latitude. One degree of latitude is about 111 km.
dream.latitude.opt.kamal: a board on a knotted cord (kamal)
dream.latitude.opt.plumb_arc: a plumb line with an arc
dream.compass.title: The needle that looks north
dream.compass.intro: You dream of a lesson: a compass needle trembles and stops. "Why does it always point north?"
dream.compass.q1.1: What will you make a needle that points north from?
dream.compass.q2.1: Where do you get a magnetic stone?
dream.compass.q3.1: The needle points north, and you need to go east. How many degrees should you turn right?
dream.compass.hint1: Physics, grade 8: iron is magnetized by a magnet.
dream.compass.breakthrough: Your "floating needle" led a caravan out of a dust storm. Merchants pay gold for it, and the ruler — for the secret.
dream.compass.partial: The needle works but lies near iron. People will buy it — cheaply.
dream.compass.failure: The needle spins every which way.
dream.compass.known: Here such a needle is already known — merchants take it on the road.
dream.compass.truth: The Chinese knew a "south-pointing" spoon of magnetite in ancient times; the sea compass is described there around 1100. In Europe the compass is mentioned around 1190, in the Islamic world around 1230.
ev.dream_intro.title: A dream of the future
ev.dream_intro.text: You had a strange dream: bright rooms, books with pictures, a teacher's voice… On waking you remember fragments — and they give you no peace.
ev.dream_intro.try.ok: You close your eyes and try to hold on to the fragments of the dream…
ev.dream_intro.skip.ok: You shrugged the dream off. By evening it was forgotten.
dream.pick_hint: Mark everything needed — how many isn't said.
dream.order_hint: Arrange with the arrows; remove the extra.
dream.mood.1: You're not sure, but you go on.
dream.mood.2: The dream fades, but you hold on to it.
dream.training.result: This was practice: the hero's life does not change. The numbers are new every time, so you can try again.
diary.dream: A dream of the future: "{dream}" — {result} ({n} of 3 steps correct).
prof.dream_alchemist.desc: Powder, fireworks and secret mixtures — at the ruler's court.
prof.dream_healer.as: a healer who knows more than anyone
prof.dream_healer.desc: Heals in ways no one here knows yet.
prof.dream_engineer.desc: Measures, builds and lifts what others can't.
prof.dream_astronomer.desc: Knows the shape of the Earth and the way by the stars.
prof.dream_banker.desc: Money works, the books balance to the coin.
dream.archimedes.death: The ruler decided you had slandered his favorite jeweler. The ruler's anger was brief — and final.
dream.numerals.title: Ten digits and a zero
dream.numerals.intro: You dream of a lesson: the teacher does long multiplication on the board, and the numbers add up as if by themselves. "Why is it so easy for us — and was so hard for merchants of old?"
dream.numerals.q2.1: What signs do you need to write any number and count fast? Mark everything needed.
dream.numerals.q3.1: Father left {total} coins to {k} brothers. How much does each get if they share equally?
dream.numerals.hint1: Maths, grade 5: multiply by each digit of the second number and add up.
dream.numerals.hint2: Just ten signs — and one of them means "nothing".
dream.numerals.hint3: Division is multiplication backwards: how many times does {k} fit into {total}?
dream.numerals.breakthrough: You taught the merchants to multiply on paper — an hour instead of a day. Noble houses now ask you to keep their accounts.
dream.numerals.partial: Counting got faster, though not everyone trusts the new signs. Neighbors come to you to check their sums.
dream.numerals.failure: The digits got tangled and the sum did not add up. People laughed — but not unkindly.
dream.numerals.known: These digits are already known here — people just believed you sooner than others.
dream.numerals.truth: Decimal notation with zero was born in India around the 6th–7th century, reached the Islamic world through Arab scholars (al-Khwarizmi, 9th century), and was described in Europe by Fibonacci in 1202 — yet Roman numerals held on there until the 15th–16th century. The Maya independently used zero in their base-20 count as early as the 4th century.
dream.numerals.opt.place_value: a digit is worth more by its place
dream.numerals.opt.letters: a letter for every hundred and thousand
dream.boiled_water.title: Boiled water
dream.boiled_water.intro: You dream of a lesson: under a microscope a drop of river water swarms with tiny creatures. "That is what killed whole cities."
dream.boiled_water.q1.1: What makes river water safe to drink? Mark everything needed.
dream.boiled_water.q2.1: Your family drinks {l} liters of water a day. How many liters should you boil for a week?
dream.boiled_water.q3.1: How do you make safe water? Arrange the steps, remove the extra.
dream.boiled_water.hint3: First clear the murk, then kill the germs — and don’t spoil the water again.
dream.boiled_water.breakthrough: Your family came through a plague while the neighbors’ children died. Now people come to you for advice — and pay for it.
dream.boiled_water.partial: Your household falls ill less often. The neighbors chuckle, but some already boil their water.
dream.boiled_water.failure: You did not do it all right, and the whole house had stomach aches.
dream.boiled_water.known: People here already drink boiled water — as tea. They just thanked you for caring.
dream.boiled_water.truth: That disease spreads through water was proven by the doctor John Snow in London in 1854, when he stopped a cholera outbreak by removing the handle of an infected pump. Louis Pasteur explained in the 1860s why boiling helps: it kills germs. In China, and from the 13th century in Japan too, the habit of drinking tea — that is, boiled water — protected people from stomach diseases for centuries.
dream.boiled_water.opt.cool_covered: let it cool under a lid
dream.boiled_water.opt.add_raw_water: top up with raw water to cool it faster
dream.field_area.title: Measuring a field
dream.field_area.intro: You dream of a lesson: a rectangle drawn on squared paper. "How many squares are inside? Count faster than one by one."
dream.field_area.q1.1: A field is {a} by {b} paces. What is its area in square paces?
dream.field_area.q2.1: Every 100 square paces need one measure of grain. How many measures for the whole field?
dream.field_area.q3.1: What do you measure the field with, so no one can cheat? Mark everything needed.
dream.field_area.hint1: Maths, grade 5: the area of a rectangle is length × width.
dream.field_area.hint3: You need something of equal length and something to mark the corners.
dream.field_area.breakthrough: You showed that the steward taxed land that wasn’t there. The lord made you a surveyor — now they call you to measure fields.
dream.field_area.partial: You got back a fair measure of grain. The neighbors ask you to measure their fields too.
dream.field_area.failure: The sums didn’t add up, and this time you paid too much.
dream.field_area.known: Surveyors here already measure fields with a rope. Your sums just confirmed theirs.
dream.field_area.truth: Field areas were computed in ancient Egypt: after the Nile flood, surveyors marked out the plots again with knotted ropes. Roman agrimensores divided land into even squares, and Chinese rules for areas appear in "The Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art" (around the 1st century). But ordinary peasants mostly measured "by eye" — and were easily cheated at tax time.
dream.field_area.opt.knotted_rope: a rope knotted at equal paces
dream.fair_price.title: A fair price
dream.fair_price.intro: You dream of a lesson: a problem about apples — "three apples cost so much; what do five cost?" Suddenly you see how often you were cheated at the market.
dream.fair_price.q1.1: {n} ells of cloth cost {c} coins. What do {m} ells cost?
dream.fair_price.q2.1: How do you check the merchant isn’t giving short weight? Mark everything needed.
dream.fair_price.q3.1: You bought 10 sacks of salt at {buy} coins and sold them at {sell}. How many coins of profit?
dream.fair_price.hint1: Maths, grade 5: first find the price of one ell.
dream.fair_price.hint2: Scales lie if one pan is heavier. What happens if you swap the goods and the weights?
dream.fair_price.hint3: The profit on a sack is the difference in prices; there are ten sacks.
dream.fair_price.breakthrough: You no longer overpay, and the guild asks you to check the scales at the market. Money flows in.
dream.fair_price.partial: You became hard to cheat. Your purse grew heavier.
dream.fair_price.failure: You got muddled in your sums and sold at a loss.
dream.fair_price.known: Merchants here already reckon by the "rule of three". You just caught up with them.
dream.fair_price.truth: The "rule of three" — finding a fourth number from three — already appears in the Chinese "Nine Chapters" (around the 1st century) and in Indian mathematics (Brahmagupta, 7th century). In Europe it was taught to merchants’ children in the Italian "abacus schools" from the 13th century. Checking scales by swapping goods and weights between the pans is an old trick against dishonest traders.
dream.fair_price.opt.standard_weights: weights stamped by the town council
dream.fair_price.opt.swap_pans: swap the goods and the weights
